/-!
# Brocard's Problem

Brocard's problem asks whether the only solutions to $n! + 1 = m^2$ are
$n = 4, 5, 7$.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brocard%27s_problem)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«398»`.
-/

reformulations.difference: The canonical theorem imported by the reviewed file expresses the no-other-solutions conjecture as equality of the set of natural-number n admitting a natural square root with {4, 5, 7}. The sources describe integer solutions of the equation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The solutions (4,5), (5,11), and (7,71) supply one containment, so set equality is equivalent to excluding all other n. Allowing n = 0 introduces no solution because 0! + 1 = 2 is not a square. Integer square roots can be replaced by their natural absolute values without changing the possible n, and a natural square root satisfying the equation is necessarily positive. These equivalences were proved in the scratch file without using the conjecture.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Quelques problèmes de la théorie des nombres (1963), problème 67, p. 129: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-14.pdf (text read via https://r.jina.ai/https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-14.pdf)
